system_description: Codex: Physics-Inspired Quantum-Integrated Developer Orchestrator with Agent Memory and Workflow Navigation

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Old memory entries are promoted/demoted based on hardcoded criteria: older_than_days=30, access_count < 3, confidence *= 0.9
sources_of_non_determinism: Datetime-based threshold uses current time (no fixed reference)
Cutoff calculated as datetime.now(UTC).isoformat()[:10] which changes daily
Access count depends on execution history between calls
Confidence decay is implicit—only happens during consolidation_memories() call, timing-dependent
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Accept optional reference_date parameter; store consolidation log with timestamps

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Patterns matched via substring search on lowercase situation string; sorted by match_score then returned in rank order
sources_of_non_determinism: Trigger matching counts substring occurrences—no seed/tie-breaking for equal matches
Score calculation: trigger_matches / len(triggers) can produce identical scores for different patterns
sort() is stable but order undefined when scores are exactly equal
Pattern candidates depend on input tags—missing tags may silently exclude valid patterns
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Add deterministic tie-breaking: pattern_id as secondary sort key; document tie behavior

non_deterministic_components.behavior: random.choices(range(len(probs)), weights=probs)[0] selects strategy probabilistically without seed control
sources_of_non_determinism: Calls random.choices without seeding—uses global random state
No reproducibility guarantee across identical game states
Can produce different strategies even with identical probability weights
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Add optional seed parameter; use numpy.random.Generator when available; document randomness contract

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Shell commands executed via subprocess.run with subprocess.PIPE, return code checked, but no timeout or deterministic retry logic
sources_of_non_determinism: Execution time varies by system load—no timeout specified
Return codes depend on external command state and environment
Error stderr/stdout captured but not validated for consistency
Command may succeed/fail based on transient system state (file locks, network, permissions)
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Add timeout parameter; validate command output against golden set; log command environment (PATH, env vars)

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Async/await event loop order; active_jobs dict order; monitoring task scheduling not deterministic
sources_of_non_determinism: asyncio.Task completion order depends on system scheduler
active_jobs.get_context dict iteration order varies (Python < 3.7) and by insertion order (3.7+)
Job status updates dependent on event loop fairness and I/O timing
WorkflowPriority enum used for ordering but no priority queue enforced—dict access order decides execution
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Use heapq-backed priority queue instead of dict; add event loop synchronization points; document async ordering contract

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Components generated in fixed order but EM field routing and prioritization depends on chaos theory generator initialization
sources_of_non_determinism: AdvancedPhysicsOrchestrator imported optionally—behavior differs if unavailable
Chaos theory generator uses ChaosNeuralNetwork (if available) which may use random initialization
Component priority values (0.7, 0.8, 1.0) hardcoded but EM field charge calculation sensitive to float precision
Fractal analysis result depends on physics_orchestrator state—not replayed from stored input
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Seed physics generators; store/replay EM field snapshots; document chaos module as optional with fallback behavior

non_deterministic_components.behavior: required_variables = {rv.name: rv for rv in _requirements} creates dict; iteration order guaranteed only in Python 3.7+
sources_of_non_determinism: Hash randomization (PYTHONHASHSEED) affects dict/set order if not controlled
Dict.keys(), .items(), .values() order varies if hash seed differs
Code relies on insertion order (Python 3.7+) but makes no guarantee for older versions
suggested_values[:5] assumes consistent ordering but depends on dict enumeration
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Use PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in test/deterministic environments; replace dict iteration with sorted() calls; add version guard

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Fatal vs non-fatal error decision is boolean flag; fallback behavior is implicit based on exception type caught
sources_of_non_determinism: log_errors decorator catches (ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError) only—other exceptions propagate unpredictably
Fatal exit (sys.exit(1)) is explicit but non-fatal handling depends on caller context
Log file rotation triggers at maxBytes boundary—exact triggering moment is timing-dependent
Context dict serialization order undefined (dict keys enumerated)
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Define exception handling matrix (exception type → action); document when exit vs retry vs raise; use OrderedDict for context

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Exponential moving average: new_rate = old_rate * (1 - alpha) + success_bool * alpha with alpha=0.1 hardcoded
sources_of_non_determinism: Confidence depends on history of calls to record_pattern_usage()—implicit state coupling
No guarantees on call order or timing between record_pattern_usage calls
Convergence depends on sequence of True/False success values—identical pattern can have different confidence based on prior invocations
No seed/version field to validate stale patterns
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Add version/generation field to patterns; snapshot state for replay; document EMA convergence properties

non_deterministic_components.behavior: How context is built, prioritized, and shaped depends on subjective judgment in OrientationResult
sources_of_non_determinism: OODA orientation step is described as 'physics-guided' but implementation uses optional components
Decision criteria implicit—no schema defines what makes context 'good' or 'relevant'
Observation selection depends on environment state not captured in logs
Planner interface abstract—concrete implementation behavior varies
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Define explicit OrientationResult schema; document decision criteria; capture observation selection rationale; version decision logic

non_deterministic_components.behavior: No explicit approval mechanism found; decisions appear to be implicit based on confidence scores and pattern matches
sources_of_non_determinism: No approval gate found in codebase—behavior determined by confidence thresholds which are context-dependent
What makes something 'approvable' is nowhere defined
Confidence cutoffs vary: min_confidence=0.0 in search_memories, but 0.5 in pattern matching
No audit trail of approval decisions
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Define approval protocol; implement audit logging; make confidence thresholds configurable and documented; add approval timestamp

non_deterministic_components.behavior: Workflow steps execute in list order, but step scheduling depends on async event loop fairness
sources_of_non_determinism: Step execution order deterministic within single workflow, but across workflows depends on priority queue fairness
No explicit scheduling algorithm documented
Timing-dependent skip/block decisions affect downstream execution
Context.working_dir may change between step invocations
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Add step scheduler with reproducible ordering; document fairness properties; snapshot context before each step

non_deterministic_components.behavior: No conflict resolution mechanism found; agent behavior assumes no conflicting goals
sources_of_non_determinism: No detection/handling of conflicting memory entries or pattern recommendations
Pattern matching may return multiple patterns with equal scores—order undefined
Component prioritization uses EM fields (if physics available) but no conflict tiebreaker specified
Implicit assumption: first match wins, but order not deterministic
non_deterministic_components.recommendation: Define conflict detection protocol; implement tiebreaker rules (e.g., timestamp, pattern_id); log conflict resolution decisions

context_dependent_behaviors.behavior: Environment variable-based decision making (AGENT_KILL_SWITCH, GITHUB_TOKEN, PYTHONHASHSEED, CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG)
dependencies: External system configuration not captured in code
Environment changes between invocations cause different behavior
No validation that environment is in expected state
examples: workflow_dispatcher.py:71 checks AGENT_KILL_SWITCH to abort startup
deterministic.py:74-75 sets PYTHONHASHSEED and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG for reproducibility

context_dependent_behaviors.behavior: Filesystem-based decision making (database paths, log rotation, temporary file creation)
dependencies: agent_memory.py:269-292 validates db_path but accepts environment variable
error_handler.py:50-52 creates logs based on current datetime (not fixed reference)
Working directory passed via context dict—changes affect subprocess execution
examples: Log rotation triggers at maxBytes boundary—timing-dependent

context_dependent_behaviors.behavior: Python version and library availability dependent behavior
dependencies: NUMPY_AVAILABLE flag gates entire physics orchestration
Fallback stubs return different results than real implementation
examples: developer_orchestrator.py:114-131 suggest_from_chaos() returns different results if numpy unavailable
quantum_game_theory.py:46-100 NumpyStub raises ImportError instead of computing results

implicit_rules.actual_criteria: created_at < cutoff AND access_count < 3 → reduce confidence by 10%
implicit_rules.not_documented: Why 30 days? Why 3 accesses? Why 0.9 multiplier? What happens at confidence < 0.3?
implicit_rules.recommendation: Document consolidation policy as explicit function with parameters; add configuration file

implicit_rules.actual_criteria: Patterns with success_rate < min_success_rate=0.5 are filtered out during match_patterns()
implicit_rules.not_documented: How is success_rate initialized? (Default 0.8 in add_pattern). How often is it updated? Does 0.5 threshold apply globally?
implicit_rules.recommendation: Store pattern configuration as versioned schema; make threshold configurable per pattern type

implicit_rules.actual_criteria: ORDER BY confidence DESC, access_count DESC LIMIT 50
implicit_rules.not_documented: Why confidence-first? Why not by created_at? Is 50 limit enforced everywhere? Can it cause stale data to be preferred?
implicit_rules.recommendation: Define search policy document; make ordering configurable; add query logging for audit

implicit_rules.actual_criteria: confidence: float 0-1; used as filter threshold but semantics undefined
implicit_rules.not_documented: What does 0.8 mean vs 0.5? Is 0.8 high or moderate? How should consumers interpret?
implicit_rules.recommendation: Define confidence levels as enum: CERTAIN (0.9+), HIGH (0.7-0.9), MEDIUM (0.5-0.7), LOW (< 0.5); use in schema

implicit_rules.actual_criteria: Step marked FAILED if returncode != 0 AND not optional; optional steps marked SKIPPED
implicit_rules.not_documented: What happens to subsequent steps after failure? Is it abort? Retry? Log and continue?
implicit_rules.recommendation: Define step execution policy (abort, retry, skip-dependent, continue); document in WorkflowStep

implicit_rules.actual_criteria: priority: 0.5-1.0 range used for EM field charge, affects routing in suggest_architecture()
implicit_rules.not_documented: How is priority assigned? Is it auto-calculated? Why 0.7, 0.8, 1.0 hardcoded?
implicit_rules.recommendation: Document priority assignment rules; add priority schema; make values configurable

human_interpretation_points.decision: Is a memory entry 'relevant' enough to retrieve?
subjective_factors: tags match user's query (no formal schema)
human_interpretation_points.how_interpreted: Implicit in search_memories() method; no criteria document
human_interpretation_points.consequence: Different threshold values produce different results; no guidance on choosing threshold

human_interpretation_points.decision: Should a pattern be used to guide the next decision?
subjective_factors: Pattern match_score (calculated from trigger word matches)
Pattern confidence (depends on when it was recorded)
human_interpretation_points.how_interpreted: Implicit in match_patterns() scoring; no documented criteria
human_interpretation_points.consequence: Identical patterns can rank differently based on invocation history; no way to audit ranking

human_interpretation_points.decision: When should a workflow step be skipped vs retried vs failed?
human_interpretation_points.how_interpreted: Implicit in WorkflowStep.execute(); no state machine defined
human_interpretation_points.consequence: Transient failures cause permanent failure; no recovery path

human_interpretation_points.decision: Which agent/component should handle this task?
human_interpretation_points.how_interpreted: Implicit in suggest_architecture(); no dispatcher algorithm documented
human_interpretation_points.consequence: Identical tasks may be routed to different components based on physics availability

human_interpretation_points.decision: Is an error fatal or recoverable?
subjective_factors: Context available at time of error
human_interpretation_points.how_interpreted: Implicit in exception type matching; fatal parameter is boolean
human_interpretation_points.consequence: Uncaught exceptions propagate unpredictably; no consistent error handling policy

timing_dependencies.impact: Consolidation run on 2025-01-01 produces different results than run on 2025-01-02 for same data
timing_dependencies.mitigation: Accept reference_date parameter; default to utcnow() but allow override

timing_dependencies.impact: Log files may be split across multiple files on high-volume days; unpredictable log path
timing_dependencies.mitigation: Use fixed-date log files; add explicit rotation trigger based on size or time

timing_dependencies.timing_factor: asyncio event loop scheduler decides which task runs next; no explicit ordering
timing_dependencies.impact: Same workflow may complete in different order across runs; jobs processed by priority but order unstable
timing_dependencies.mitigation: Use explicit priority queue; add synchronization points; document fairness properties

timing_dependencies.timing_factor: No timeout; command duration depends on system load, I/O availability, permission state
timing_dependencies.impact: Same command may succeed/fail based on system state; no reproducibility guarantee
timing_dependencies.mitigation: Add timeout and retry logic; validate output against golden set; log environment state

timing_dependencies.impact: Strategy selection differs across runs; identical game state produces different moves
timing_dependencies.mitigation: Accept optional seed parameter; use numpy.random.Generator with explicit seed; log seed used

determinism_blockers: Quantum game theory uses probabilistic strategy selection by design (intentional randomness)
Async/await event loop scheduling is inherently non-deterministic (system scheduler dependent)
Subprocess execution depends on external command behavior and system state
OODA orientation step is described as subjective human-in-the-loop decision
Memory consolidation depends on historical access patterns and timing
determinism_improvements_possible: Add seed parameter to quantum_game_theory strategy selection
Replace async dict-based job queue with deterministic priority queue
Document and parameterize all implicit thresholds (confidence, access_count, consolidation criteria)
Add audit logging for all decision points (pattern selection, memory retrieval, component routing)
Define formal approval/conflict resolution protocols with explicit tiebreakers
Add reference_date parameters to time-dependent operations
Snapshot and replay context for debugging non-deterministic behavior
confidence_rationale: Analysis based on static code inspection of agent memory, orchestrator, workflow dispatcher, and deterministic utilities. Physical examination of source code shows clear patterns of non-deterministic behavior. Confidence reduced because OODA orientation and actual agent dispatch logic are in cognitive_brain module (not fully analyzed here). Some behaviors are documented as intentional (quantum randomness, EMA decay). High-confidence areas: memory consolidation logic, pattern matching, workflow execution. Medium-confidence: async scheduling, error handling (may have additional fallbacks not shown). Low-confidence: approval logic (not found—may be implicit in decision trees)
analysis_notes: This analysis focuses on code-level non-determinism sources, not runtime behavior variability
Intentional randomness (quantum_game_theory) is flagged but may be acceptable for decision exploration
Several components are marked 'optional' (numpy, advanced_physics)—behavior differs based on availability
No approval mechanism found; decisions appear implicit based on confidence/pattern matching
Implicit rules discovered by reading code—no formal specification document found
Memory consolidation is the most clearly non-deterministic feature (date-based culling)
Async workflow orchestrator has subtle ordering issues due to dict-based job storage
Error handling uses implicit exception type matching—coverage gaps likely
